function: system: area-7 over-the-air FL aggregation on single-antenna devices and server, no RIS; p. 3, eq. (5): 'hk(n) ~ CN(0, 1) represents the k-th Rayleigh fading channel coefficient'.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2305.05933v2 (p. 1), the preprint of 'Spectrum Breathing: Protecting Over-the-Air Federated Learning Against Interference' by Wang, Huang and Eldar, which matches the DOI. Checks 1 to 5 pass: a research article that proposes and evaluates a method; over-the-air FL, so the CNN trained across the devices is the learned element (p. 9: 'The task is to train a CNN model having 21,840 parameters'); the design is a physical-layer AirComp transceiver of random gradient pruning, truncated channel inversion and spread spectrum (p. 4-5, Fig. 2); its problem is the over-the-air aggregation itself, measured by the AirComp error (p. 3, eq. 6; p. 7, eq. 23), hence area 7. The interference comes 'from neighboring cells or jammers' (p. 1), but it is suppressed inside the aggregation design, so I did not read the work as anti-jamming (function); reviewer to confirm. Check 6 applies: every device and the server have a single antenna and there is no RIS. p. 3, eq. (5): 'hk(n) ~ CN(0, 1) represents the k-th Rayleigh fading channel coefficient' (scalar channel, scalar received chip); p. 5, eq. (13): scalar truncated channel inversion pk(n) = sqrt(P0)/hk(n) when |hk(n)|^2 >= Gth, and Fig. 2 draws one antenna at the device and one at the server; p. 9: 'one server and 10 devices' and 'all channel coefficients are modelled as CN(0, 1) random variables'. The IRS appears only in related work (p. 1, ref. [24]) and MIMO beamforming only as a future extension in the conclusion (p. 11). The work is neither OTFS nor NTN, so no single-antenna exemption. Quantitative results exist (p. 10, validation accuracy on MNIST versus communication time), so check 7 would not apply.
